declined.reason: Declined in the suggested form: 一口に means 'all at once,' not only 'one mouthful' – the man had already eaten; 'in a single mouthful' misplaces the idiom. Already amended minimally to 'unable to put anything into words' on R12's evidence; no further change.

disagreements.choice: F9: the picture is reflected in the bottom of her eyes, keeping the Japanese optical image rather than flattening it or relocating it 'deep in' the eyes.
disagreements.faithful_side: F9: 映ってゐた means the far picture was reflected in the bottom of her eyes, not merely lying there.
disagreements.readable_side: R11: 'bottom of her eyes' and 'was to be seen' are anatomically and syntactically awkward in English.

disagreements.choice: Neither the faithful reader's proposed 'stood reflected' nor the readable reader's 'could still be seen' is adopted; the gnomic summary remains 'would be forever before a rest like night,' preserving the Japanese refusal to specify posture or doctrine.
disagreements.faithful_side: F6: ある means simply 'be'; English 'stand forever' imports a posture and turns the summary into a tableau.
disagreements.readable_side: No readable-reader note on this span; the accessible English temptation would be to clarify the image into standing before rest.

data.say:
I made the smaller, text-led changes and left the vision's diction unexalted.

Declined:
- R2: declined. The suggested rewrite loses the repeated Japanese structure of tiredness being seen in the eyes and about the shoulders; the slightly stiff repetition carries the shared young exhaustion, so the text wins over smoother phrasing.
- R3: declined. “All of the child” keeps the Japanese totalising すべて and its repetition chain into the vision; changing it to “everything in the child” would clarify and weaken that network.
- R17: declined as an added attribution. The Japanese gives p36 no speaker tag, and adding “the man said” would clarify what the narration leaves carried by voice and sequence; the line remains unattributed as in the source.

Disagreements and unsettled places:
- p18, F9 against R11: the faithful reader is right that 映ってゐた is “reflected,” and the readable reader is right that “lay” was inert; I chose “was reflected dark and quiet in the bottom of her eyes.” The reading settles this in favour of keeping the eye-bottom picture, so it does not go up.
- p17, F6: I removed “stand” because ある is only “be,” and kept “would be forever before a rest like night” unresolved rather than turning the summary into a posture or a doctrine. This is settled by the reading and does not go up.

Nothing in this part changes an earlier part.

House log: The desk kept the potato hard and nasty, the picture reflected rather than explained, and the final return to work and storm unexalted.
